# API Tokens

Version 0.3.0 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

> Walkthrough for app owners: [API tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens). This page is the technical reference.

Long-lived API tokens for your app: secrets that start with `pbt_`, for CI, deploys, scripts and agents. Each token
belongs to an account and acts as that account. It can be limited to scopes, given an expiry, and revoked on its own.
Send one as `Authorization: Bearer pbt_…`. Ordinary PocketBase auth tokens keep working unchanged.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Tokens is built into `pocketone` and always on. There's nothing to install or turn on.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
tokens.MustRegister(app, apitokens.Config{})
app.Start()
```

To use `$apiTokens` in `pb_hooks`, bind it in jsvm's `OnInit` (the stock binary does):

```go
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { tokens.BindJS(app, rt) }})
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/api-tokens`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or environment variable for Tokens. In `pocketone`:
- any account (a superuser, or a record of any auth collection) can own tokens;
- a token never expires unless you give it an expiry.

A Go build can narrow both (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Scopes

A token without scopes has its owner's full rights. A token with scopes works only on the requests its scopes cover,
plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); anywhere else it gets `403`. Extensions, contracts and your own
`pb_hooks` register the scopes. In `pocketone` they are:

| Scope | From | Allows | Who can hold it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deploy` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Deploy code (hooks, migrations, pages, public files, packages), read files and logs | superusers |
| `deploy:read` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Read deployed files and stream logs | superusers |
| `<name>`, `<name>:read` | each [contract](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) the app provides | That contract's operations under `/api/_c/<id>/`: `remote` and `remote:read`, `restore` and `restore:read`, `settings` and `settings:read`, `bulkmail:read`, `cache`, ... | per contract |

Contract scopes are registered when the app serves, so **Settings → API tokens** on the running app lists every
scope. The `pocketone token` command works offline and doesn't see them: `token scopes` lists only `deploy` and
`deploy:read`, and `token create --scope restore` fails with `unknown scope "restore"`. Create a token with a
contract scope from the dashboard or the [REST API](#rest-api-api-tokensv1).

### Your own scopes

Declare a scope at the top level of a `pb_hooks` file. It then shows up in **Settings → API tokens** and on
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth)'s consent page:

```js
// pb_hooks/scopes.pb.js
$apiTokens.registerScope({
  name: 'notes:read',                        // lower-case letters, digits, ":" and "_"
  description: 'Read notes',                 // shown in the token screen and on the consent page
  paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'], // URL prefixes where a token holding it works
  methods: ['GET'],                          // optional: only these methods (GET covers HEAD)
})
$apiTokens.registerScope({ name: 'notes:write', description: 'Change notes', paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'] })
```

- `collections: ['users']` limits which accounts may hold the scope.
- Registering a name again merges its paths, methods and collections, so reloading hooks is safe.
- Two names whose headers would be the same (`notes:write` and `notes_write`) can't both be registered.

Check a scope on your own route:

```js
routerAdd('POST', '/api/notes/archive', (e) => { /* ... */ }, $apis.requireAuth(), $apiTokens.requireScope('notes:write'))
```

`$apiTokens.requireScope` refuses a signed-out request, and a token that doesn't hold the scope. Inside a handler,
`$apiTokens.hasScope(e, 'notes:write')` tells you the same.

Check a scope in a collection API rule. Every signed-in request carries `X-Token-Scope-<Name>: 1` for each scope it
holds, and rules read it as `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>` (`:` becomes `_`):

```
@request.auth.id = owner && @request.headers.x_token_scope_notes_write = "1"
```

- A PocketBase auth token or an unscoped API token holds every registered scope (except ones its collection can't
  hold).
- A scoped token holds only its own scopes. A signed-out request holds none.
- Headers a client sends with that prefix are always dropped, so they can't be forged.

`$apiTokens.ruleField('notes:write')` returns the rule field for a name, and `$apiTokens.scopes()` lists every registered
scope with its header and rule field.

### Scopes with values

A scope can let a token hold it for some values only, such as some record ids. The token's scope list then says
`name=value`, once per value (`notes=abc123`, `notes=def456`). The bare name still means every value. Declare the
values when you register the scope:

```js
$apiTokens.registerScope({
  name: 'notes',
  description: 'Your notes',
  paths: ['/api/notes/'],
  values: { description: 'a note id' }, // shown in the token screen
})
```

Paths and methods don't look at values: a token holding `notes=abc123` authenticates on every path `notes` covers. Your
route checks the value:

```js
routerAdd('GET', '/api/notes/{id}', (e) => {
  if (!$apiTokens.hasScope(e, 'notes', e.request.pathValue('id'))) throw new ForbiddenError('Not this note.')
  // ...
}, $apis.requireAuth())
```

- `$apiTokens.hasScope(e, name, value)` is true for the bare scope, for `name=value`, and for a PocketBase auth token or
  an unscoped token. Without a value it's true when the request holds the scope for any value.
- `$apiTokens.scopeValues(e, name)` returns `{ all: true }` for every value, or `{ all: false, values: [...] }`.
- The scope's header carries the values instead of `1` (`X-Token-Scope-Notes: abc123,def456`), so a rule's `= "1"` still
  means every value.
- A value is 1–200 letters, digits and `. _ : @ / + -`. A scope registered without `values` refuses `name=value`.
- In Go, `Values: &apitokens.ScopeValues{Description: "...", Check: func(owner, value) error}` adds a check when a token
  is created (for example, that the owner owns that record).

## Use

### From the dashboard

1. Open **Settings → API tokens** (under **Access**). Only superusers see this screen.
2. Fill in a **Name**. Optionally set **Expires in (days)**, and tick any **Scopes** (none means full rights). A
   scope that takes values shows a box when ticked: leave it empty for every value, or list some, comma-separated.
3. By default the token is yours. To make one for another account, fill in **Owner collection** (default
   `_superusers`) and **Owner (id or email)**.
4. Click **Create token**. Copy the token now: it's shown only once and never stored.

The list shows each token's name, its first characters, owner, scopes, expiry and when it was last used (time and IP).
Tokens issued by [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth) carry an `oauth: <client id>` label. Click **Revoke** and
confirm to delete one; anything using it stops working at once.

App users who aren't superusers manage their own tokens through the [REST API](#rest-api-api-tokensv1).

### From the command line

The `token` command works on the local data dir, like `superuser`, so you can set up tokens before the first serve:

```bash
pocketone token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci --scope deploy --ttl 720h   # prints the secret
pocketone token create --collection users --record user@example.com --name script
pocketone token list                                    # every token, or one owner's with an owner flag
pocketone token revoke <id> [<id>...]
pocketone token revoke --all --superuser admin@example.com
pocketone token scopes
```

Pick the owner with `--superuser <email>`, or `--collection <name> --record <id or email>`. `--scope` can be repeated,
and takes `name=value` for a scope with values; without `--ttl` the token never expires.

### Using a token

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_…" https://myapp.example.com/api/collections/notes/records
```

- An invalid, revoked or expired token leaves the request signed out, like an invalid PocketBase token.
- A scoped token used outside its scopes gets `403` ("This API token's scopes (…) don't allow this request.").
- A token can't be exchanged for a PocketBase auth token (`auth-refresh` and `impersonate` refuse it), so revoking a
  token really ends its access.
- Expired tokens are deleted once a day. Deleting an account deletes its tokens.

### In the logs

- A rejected token is logged at debug level: `tokens: rejected API token`.
- The daily cleanup logs `tokens: deleted expired tokens` with a count when it deletes any, and
  `tokens: delete expired` as a warning if it fails.

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone oauth clients add`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-add) | Registers a client (prints its id, and its secret once for a confidential client) |
| [`pocketone oauth clients list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-list) | Lists registered clients |
| [`pocketone oauth clients rm <client_id>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-oauth-clients-rm) | Removes a client |
| [`pocketone token create`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-create) | Creates an API token and prints its secret (shown once) |
| [`pocketone token list`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-list) | Lists API tokens (all, or one owner's) |
| [`pocketone token revoke [id...]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-revoke) | Revokes API tokens by id, or all of one owner's (--all) |
| [`pocketone token scopes`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-token-scopes) | Lists the scopes extensions registered |

### [api-tokens.verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [verify](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1#verify) | `pocketone remote api-tokens verify --token <value> --ip <value>` | `POST /api/_c/api-tokens.verify/v1` | `api-tokens_verify_verify` |

### [api-tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens/v1)

Its HTTP API under `/api/_c/api-tokens/v1/`, as the contract describes.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Its access tokens are API tokens, issued with the client's id, the granted scopes and, when asked for, an audience. They show up under Settings → API tokens and can be revoked there. The OAuth server needs Tokens on the app. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | An agent's OAuth sign-in to `/mcp` is an API token bound to `/mcp` that never expires; revoke it to disconnect the agent. Tool calls run as the token's owner. A full-access token's calls hold every registered scope; a token limited to scopes on the consent page has its calls checked like requests with those scopes (`WithScopes`). |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Registers `deploy` and `deploy:read`; a `deploy` token is what CI uses. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | `pocketone login` takes a pasted API token when the remote has no OAuth server. In CI, put a token in `P1_TOKEN`. remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`) reports a token's id and scopes, whatever its scopes. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | It's a standard member, so every instance gets its own tokens, routes and screen; reconfigure it on the host's set with `set.APITokens = apitokens.New(apitokens.Config{...})`. With Pocker, per instance, `extensions: {api-tokens: {enabled: false}}` turns it off and `collections: [...]` picks who may own tokens. |

### Building on Tokens

**Register a scope from Go.** Extensions register their scopes on the app, usually on bootstrap, and guard their routes:

```go
tk := tokens.For(app)
tk.MustRegisterScope(tokens.Scope{
    Name:        "notes:write",
    Description: "Change notes",
    Paths:       []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"},
    Methods:     []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}, // optional
    Collections: []string{"users"},                   // optional: who may hold it
})
se.Router.POST("/api/notes/archive", h).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), tokens.RequireScope("notes:write"))
```

- **Guards.** A Go scope can add `Match func(*core.RequestEvent) bool`: a token with the scope also works on any
  request it returns true for. It runs before the owner is loaded, so it may look only at the request.
- **Shared scopes.** Registering a name again merges its paths, methods, guards and collections, so several extensions
  can share one scope.
- **Scope values.** `Values: &tokens.ScopeValues{Description, Check}` lets a token hold a scope for some values only
  (`notes=abc123`). `Check(owner, value)` runs when a token is created; an error refuses it. Routes check the value
  with `tokens.HasScopeFor(e, "notes", id)`, or list them with `tokens.ValuesFor(e, "notes")` (`all` is true for every
  value). Through the contract: `grant.HasScopeFor`, `grant.ScopeValues`, and `apitokensv1.SplitScope` /
  `JoinScope` for the `name=value` form.
- **Read the token on a request.** `tokens.FromRequest(e)` returns the token a request used (nil for a PocketBase
  auth token), with its `Owner`, `Scopes` and `Audience`. `tokens.HasScope(e, "x")` is true for PocketBase auth
  tokens and unscoped API tokens.
- **Without importing this package.** Other extensions use the [api-tokens/v1](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/api-tokens/v1/tokens.go)
  contract instead: `tokensv1.Contract.Of(app)` registers scopes (`RegisterScope`), lists them and checks `Reaches`;
  `tokensv1.FromRequest(e)` is the request's token (its `Grant`: owner, scopes, audience, client id);
  `tokensv1.WithScopes` limits in-process requests. Deploy and MCP work this way. The `X-Token-Scope-*` headers work
  for rules and JS.
- **Audience.** A token created with `CreateOptions.Audience` (the OAuth server sets it from the RFC 8707 `resource`
  parameter) only works under that URL's path, plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); elsewhere it gets `403`. When the audience has
  a path (like `https://host/mcp`), the token works there whatever its scopes: the scopes limit what that endpoint
  does on the token's behalf (MCP passes them on with `WithScopes`), not the endpoint itself.
- **Limit in-process requests.** `tokens.WithScopes(ctx, scopes)` returns a context whose requests are checked like a
  token limited to `scopes`, whatever credential they carry: `403` where the scopes don't reach, and only those
  scopes in the `X-Token-Scope-*` headers and `HasScope`. Requests made inside them with the same context inherit
  the limit, and a nested `WithScopes` only narrows it. No client value can set it. `tokens.ScopesFromContext(ctx)`
  reads it. `Reaches(scopes, method, pattern)` says whether scopes could cover a route pattern (`{name}` segments
  match anything), and `Scope.Infrastructure()` whether a scope only reaches contract APIs (`/api/_c/`).

**Go API.** `tokens.For(app)` returns the service: `Create(owner, CreateOptions{Name, Scopes, Expires, ClientId,
Audience})` returns the secret and record; also `Verify(secret)`, `List(owner)`, `Get(id)`, `Revoke(id)`,
`RevokeAll(owner)`, `DeleteExpired()`, `RegisterScope`, `MustRegisterScope`, `Scopes()`, `Collections()` and
`AllowedCollection(c)`. `tokens.BindJS(vm, app)` adds `$apiTokens`; the extkit extension (`tokens.New`) also binds it.

**JS.** `$apiTokens.registerScope({name, description, paths, methods, collections})`, `$apiTokens.requireScope(name)`,
`$apiTokens.hasScope(e, name)`, `$apiTokens.ruleField(name)` and `$apiTokens.scopes()`.

### REST API (api-tokens/v1)

The [api-tokens/v1](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/api-tokens/v1/tokens.go) contract, at `/api/_c/api-tokens/v1`. Any signed-in account; superusers
see and manage everyone's.

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/api-tokens/v1` | Your tokens. Superusers see all, or one owner's with `?ownerCollection=&owner=`. |
| `POST /api/_c/api-tokens/v1` | `{name, scopes, ttl \| expires}` (`ttl` in seconds, `expires` RFC 3339); superusers may add `ownerCollection` and `owner`. Returns the secret once. A scoped token can only create tokens within its own scopes. |
| `DELETE /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/{id}` | Revoke one. |
| `POST /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/revoke-all` | Revoke all of yours (superusers: `{ownerCollection, owner}`). |
| `GET /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/scopes` | The registered scopes, who may own tokens, and whether you can. |

Owners can also list, view and delete their own tokens through the records API of `_api_tokens_tokens`.

### Checking a token from another server (api-tokens.verify/v1)

A server that a client hands one of this app's tokens to (a host in front of the app's accounts) asks the app what
the token allows with the [api-tokens.verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1) contract:
`POST /api/_c/api-tokens.verify/v1` with `{"token": "pbt_...", "ip": "<client address>"}`, as a superuser (scope
`api_tokens_verify`). The answer is `{"valid": true, "grant": {...}}` with the owner and the scopes (values included),
or `{"valid": false, "reason": "invalid" | "expired"}`. In Go, `verifyv1.NewClient(appURL, superuserToken, nil)`.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/api-tokens/example/main.go) runs one app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens, the token API (`/api/_c/api-tokens/v1`) and the `token` command.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens in the dashboard, the token API (/api/_c/api-tokens/v1)
// and the `token` command.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci
//	curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_..." http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/api-tokens"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	tk := apitokens.MustRegister(app, apitokens.Config{
		Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens
	})
	// an extension's scope: a token limited to "hello" only authenticates under /api/hello; a JWT or unscoped token
	// holds it too, and every request that holds it carries X-Token-Scope-Hello: 1 for rules and hooks
	tk.MustRegisterScope(apitokens.Scope{Name: "hello", Description: "Say hello", Paths: []string{"/api/hello"}, Methods: []string{"GET"}})

	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"hello": e.Auth.Email()})
		}).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), apitokens.RequireScope("hello"))
		return se.Next()
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Go config

```go
tokens.MustRegister(app, apitokens.Config{
    Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens (default: every auth collection)
    MaxTTL:      0,                                // cap on a token's lifetime (0: none)
})
```

With `MaxTTL` set, a token asked for with no expiry or a later one gets the cap instead. If you narrow `Collections`,
The OAuth server can only sign in accounts of those collections.

### Bringing tokens from another system

To keep tokens another system issued working (their owners already hold the secrets), register their prefix and
store each one with `Import`, which keeps only its hash, as `Create` does:

```go
tk.RegisterPrefix("ph_pat_") // pbt_ is always registered
rec, err := tk.Import(owner, "ph_pat_…", apitokens.CreateOptions{Name: "ci", Scopes: []string{"deploy"}})
```

Every registered prefix is checked the same way: a secret starts with one and has at least 32 characters after it.
`Import` takes a `pbt_` secret too (a token moving from another app). The one difference: tokens the app creates
always start with `pbt_`. A prefix is lower-case letters, digits and `_`, ends with `_`, and can't overlap one
already registered. The old system's hash is usually of something else, so import a secret when it's next used
(check it the old way, then `Import` it), not ahead of time.

## How it works

- Tokens live in the `_api_tokens_tokens` collection: owner (collection id and record id), name, `hash` (SHA-256 of the secret;
  the secret itself is never stored), display prefix, scopes, expiry, last use (time and IP), OAuth client id and
  audience.
- The bearer check is a middleware that runs just before PocketBase's own auth middleware; a second one, right after
  it, sets the scope headers. Last use is written at most once a minute per token.
- [`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/api-tokens/example/main.go) runs one app where superusers and users may own tokens, with a `hello` scope
  for `GET /api/hello`. Try it with `go run ./example serve` and
  `go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci` (logins from
  [devusers](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go): admin@example.com / password, user@example.com / password).
